payload.headline: Amazon falls 3.87% to 257.37, back inside value range; still waiting for 238.65

summary.thesis: Margins are improving, but growth is slowing, cash flow is negative, and the price still sits above the middle of its own valuation range.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 238.65; swing: no trade while the price sits in the middle of its range with no trend.
summary.act_at: Buy at 238.65; small first entry at 245.03 only if free cash flow improves

payload.happening: Amazon fell 3.87% to 257.37. That gives back yesterday's jump to 267.74 and puts the price back in its usual zone of 255.19–259.49, next to the 20-day average of 257.48. CNBC reported that Amazon will bid for the 2030 men's World Cup rights and that it launched an in-app campaign against a New York City delivery bill (the second report is unconfirmed). The data shows no earnings date.
payload.business: Today's news doesn't change the business. A World Cup bid is a content spending decision, and it's only a bid. The New York delivery bill campaign is about rules and public image, and the report is unconfirmed. Neither shows up in today's numbers. The numbers that matter come from the last filing (2026-10-30). Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, and the gross margin is 51.37%. Profitability is not what's at risk. The risks are growth and cash. Sales growth versus a year earlier slowed to 12.09% this quarter from 16.61% two quarters ago. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, swung to -46.9B over 12 months from 10.6B a year before. Debt is 180.9B against 55.8B of cash, so net cash is -66.7B, though liquidity of 114.2B leaves room to keep going. The filings flag that unpaid customer bills rose 61% while quarterly sales rose 12%. That can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying slower. Net margin (16.9%) is above operating margin (13.09%). That means part of reported profit comes from outside day-to-day operations, which tends to be less repeatable (general knowledge). Analysts expect next-year EPS of 10.67, below this year's 12.8, which fits that reading.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow (DCF) value, because free cash flow is negative. The only method left compares today's price-to-sales ratio (price divided by sales per share) with Amazon's own last 5 years. That gives 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 266.4 at the high end. At 257.37 the price is inside the range again but above the middle. Price-to-sales is 3.5, which is at the 82nd percentile of its own 5-year history. Against peers the stock looks cheap: the peer median is 6.6, and the growth-adjusted ratio versus peers is 0.63. Which comparison you trust drives the whole gap. The filing risk notes say the price needs about 34% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. On earnings, the price is 20.9 times trailing EPS but 24.1 times next year's lower estimate.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range instead of moving toward the peer median of 6.6.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now keeps more profit.
Trailing sales reached 797.5B, up from 691.3B, and analysts expect 959.6B next year.
At 3.5 times sales against a peer median of 6.6 (growth-adjusted 0.63), Amazon is cheaper than its large tech peers.
bear: Free cash flow was -46.9B over 12 months, down from 10.6B, and net cash is -66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while the filings say the price needs about 34% a year.
Next-quarter EPS estimates were cut 2.6% in 30 days, and next-year EPS of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8.

levels.what: Top of the own-history value range. No buying above it.
The 200-day average, just above the 238.97–244.73 support zone. A small first entry here only if the next filing shows free cash flow better than -46.9B.
Middle of the own-history value range, where price meets fair value. This is the main buy level.

longterm.why: The price is back inside the range but still above fair value, while growth slows and cash burns. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: At 257.37 the price is in the middle of its range, with support at 246.35–251.93 below and resistance starting at 261.12 above. A typical day's move (the ATR, or average daily range) is 9.61, so there is no room for a good gain-to-risk trade. All three averages are flat and the macro view is a tech downtrend. There is no trade unless the price pulls back into 246.35–251.93 and holds, or closes above 268.76.

decision.timing: With no earnings date in the data, price levels set the timing. Options to 2026-12-18 price in a move of about 8.3%, with implied volatility (44.4) a little above recent actual volatility (41.3).

change_mind: A filing that shows 12-month free cash flow better than -46.9B while the price is near 245.03 would justify a small first buy.
Quarterly sales growth falling below 12.09%, or next-quarter EPS coming in under the low estimate of 1.98, would turn the stance from wait to avoid.
A close above 268.76 with the 20-day and 50-day averages turning up would reopen a swing setup, even though that is above the 266.4 value ceiling.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. Today's drop to 257.37 took the price back inside the value range but left it above the 238.65 midpoint, and the free cash flow of -46.9B that drove yesterday's call has not changed.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
